Summary: US-01 Compare each migrated output row for row
Description: As the finance owner, I want every migrated report compared row for row with its legacy output, so that I can retire the legacy report without re-checking it by hand. Requirement: FR-02.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a parallel run where Fabric matches legacy exactly, when the validator runs, then the verdict is GO. [runs: tests/test_parallel_run_validation.py::test_clean_parallel_run_is_go]
2. Given a Fabric output missing one legacy row, when the validator runs, then the verdict is NO-GO and names the failing check. [runs: tests/test_parallel_run_validation.py::test_dropped_row_is_nogo]
3. Given one value shifted on one row, when the validator runs, then the verdict is NO-GO. [runs: tests/test_parallel_run_validation.py::test_shifted_value_is_nogo]
4. Given two errors that cancel out in the column total, when the validator runs, then the verdict is still NO-GO. [runs: tests/test_parallel_run_validation.py::test_offsetting_errors_still_caught]
5. Given a key present in Fabric but not in legacy, when the validator runs, then the verdict is NO-GO. [runs: tests/test_parallel_run_validation.py::test_extra_key_is_nogo]

Summary: US-02 An empty output never passes
Description: As the technical lead, I want an empty extract never to count as a match, so that a broken load cannot be signed off because both sides were blank. Requirement: FR-03.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given both legacy and Fabric outputs are empty, when the validator runs, then the verdict is not GO. [runs: tests/test_validator_edge_cases.py::test_two_empty_outputs_are_not_a_go]
2. Given only one side is empty, when the validator runs, then the verdict is not GO. [runs: tests/test_validator_edge_cases.py::test_one_side_empty_is_not_a_go]
3. Given a duplicated key on one side, when the validator runs, then the duplicate is caught. [runs: tests/test_validator_edge_cases.py::test_duplicate_key_on_one_side_is_caught]

Summary: US-03 Same numbers, whatever the formatting
Description: As the metric owner, I want formatting and row-order differences ignored but any real difference caught to the cent, so that users keep exactly the approved numbers and the gate does not cry wolf. Requirement: BR-03.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the same values stored as different numeric types, when checksums are compared, then they match. [runs: tests/test_parallel_run_validation.py::test_checksum_ignores_dtype_formatting]
2. Given the same rows in a different order, when the validator runs, then the verdict is GO. [runs: tests/test_validator_edge_cases.py::test_row_order_does_not_matter]
3. Given integer and float representations of one amount, when the validator runs, then they agree. [runs: tests/test_validator_edge_cases.py::test_integer_and_float_representations_agree]
4. Given a sub-cent rounding difference, when the validator runs, then the gate does not fail. [runs: tests/test_validator_edge_cases.py::test_sub_cent_rounding_does_not_fail_the_gate]
5. Given a difference of one cent, when the validator runs, then the gate fails. [runs: tests/test_validator_edge_cases.py::test_the_gate_is_cent_exact_not_merely_within_a_cent]
6. Given a quantity that drifts while amounts match, when the validator runs, then the drift is caught. [runs: tests/test_validator_edge_cases.py::test_quantity_drift_alone_is_caught]

Summary: US-04 GO means every check passed
Description: As the business owner, I want GO only when every check passes, with totals reported per column, so that one green check cannot hide a red one. Requirement: FR-03.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given any single check fails, when the verdict is formed, then it is NO-GO. [runs: tests/test_validator_edge_cases.py::test_verdict_is_conjunctive]
2. Given a completed run, when the result is reported, then control totals appear per column. [runs: tests/test_validator_edge_cases.py::test_control_totals_are_reported_per_column]
3. Given a NO-GO in a scheduled wave, when retirement is requested, then it is refused until a GO is recorded. [manual: UAT scenario owned by the technical lead]

Summary: US-05 One record per artifact
Description: As the programme manager, I want every artifact to carry its status, wave, owner, planned and actual effort, so that progress reports show what the data supports. Requirement: FR-01.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the generated programme register, when it is loaded, then every artifact links to a valid wave, owner and blocker. [runs: tests/test_migration_program_data.py::test_referential_integrity]
2. Given any artifact, when its status is read, then it is one of the allowed statuses. [runs: tests/test_migration_program_data.py::test_statuses_valid]
3. Given an artifact marked Done, when its effort is read, then actual effort is recorded. [runs: tests/test_migration_program_data.py::test_done_artifacts_have_actuals]

Summary: US-06 Done means proven
Description: As the programme manager, I want an artifact marked Done only after a GO, so that "done" in a status report means "validated", not "deployed". Requirement: FR-03.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an artifact marked Done, when its validation history is read, then its last verdict is GO. [runs: tests/test_migration_program_data.py::test_done_artifacts_end_on_go]
2. Given any NO-GO verdict, when its reason is read, then the reason matches the failing check. [runs: tests/test_migration_program_data.py::test_verdict_reason_consistency]

Summary: US-07 Every visual can be read without seeing it
Description: As a report user who relies on a screen reader, I want every visual to carry alt text that describes that visual, so that I get the same information as everyone else. Requirement: proposed NFR-04, accessibility (not yet in the register).
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given any visual in the Power BI project, when the report is built, then it has alt text. [runs: tests/test_every_visual_has_alt_text.py::test_every_visual_has_alt_text]
2. Given a visual's alt text, when it is read, then it describes that visual, not a generic label. [runs: tests/test_every_visual_has_alt_text.py::test_alt_text_describes_this_visual]

Summary: US-08 Filters say what they cannot filter
Description: As a report user, I want a visual that a slicer cannot reach to say so, so that I do not read an unfiltered number as a filtered one. Requirement: FR-01.
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Given a slicer and a visual it cannot filter, when the page is built, then the visual states its scope. [runs: tests/test_slicer_scope_is_visible.py::test_every_visual_a_slicer_cannot_reach_says_so]

Summary: US-09 Dates cover the whole programme
Description: As a report user, I want the calendar to cover every month the programme touches, so that no wave silently falls outside a date filter. Requirement: FR-01.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the programme's dated files, when the calendar is derived, then every joined month lies inside it. [runs: tests/test_the_calendar_covers_the_programme.py::test_every_joined_month_lies_inside_the_span_the_calendar_derives]
2. Given the calendar definition, when it is read, then it is not pinned to a literal date. [runs: tests/test_the_calendar_covers_the_programme.py::test_the_calendar_is_not_pinned_to_a_literal_date]

Summary: US-10 Tamper-evident release evidence
Description: As the release reviewer, I want the release packet's evidence hashed and verifiable, so that what was approved is provably what was tested. Requirement: NFR-03.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the release packet, when it is checked, then every required evidence file is present and hashed. [runs: tests/test_production_readiness.py::test_required_evidence_is_present_and_integrity_hashed]
2. Given an edited evidence file, when the digest is verified, then the tampering is detected. [runs: tests/test_production_readiness.py::test_packet_digest_verifies_and_detects_tampering]

Summary: US-11 Approve only what was reviewed
Description: As the release reviewer, I want the packet to approve only the public synthetic demo and keep authentication, telemetry and live Fabric open, so that no one reads a demo approval as a production one. Requirement: NFR-01.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the release packet, when its scope is read, then it approves only the public synthetic demo. [runs: tests/test_production_readiness.py::test_release_packet_approves_only_the_public_synthetic_demo]
2. Given the release packet, when open reviews are listed, then authentication, telemetry and live Fabric are still open. [runs: tests/test_production_readiness.py::test_packet_keeps_auth_telemetry_and_live_fabric_as_open_reviews]

Summary: US-12 Every user group hears before its wave
Description: As the change lead, I want each affected user group to receive role-specific communication before its wave, so that nobody meets the new report on cutover morning. Requirement: CHG-01.
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Given a scheduled wave, when the communication register is checked a week before, then every affected group shows a delivered message. [manual: target in the [change and adoption plan](CHANGE_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN.md), not claimed as achieved]

Summary: US-13 Cutover can be undone in time
Description: As the technical lead, I want a rehearsed rollback that completes inside the recovery window, so that a failed cutover costs hours, not a month-end. Requirement: NFR-02.
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Given a rehearsal cutover that fails, when rollback is run from the [cutover runbook](../cutover_runbook.md), then legacy service resumes inside the agreed window. [manual: rehearsal scenario owned by the technical lead]

Summary: US-14 Every artifact has an owner before it moves
Description: As the business owner, I want each artifact's owner, purpose, criticality and consumers recorded before it is scheduled, so that someone can accept or refuse it. Requirement: BR-01.
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Given the artifact inventory, when completeness is reported, then 100% of artifacts carry owner, purpose, criticality and consumers. [manual: designed control in this pack; not implemented as a production records system]

Summary: US-15 Month-end never goes dark
Description: As the finance owner, I want waves scheduled around a blackout calendar, so that month-end and statutory outputs stay available throughout. Requirement: BR-02.
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Given the approved blackout calendar, when a wave is scheduled, then no cutover falls inside a blackout window. [manual: UAT scenario owned by the finance owner]

Summary: US-16 Users are ready before GO
Description: As the business owner, I want required users and service-desk analysts to finish their preparation before a wave goes live, so that support is not learning the service from the first ticket. Requirement: CHG-02.
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Given a wave's readiness review, when completion is checked, then at least 90% of required users are prepared and no critical role is unsupported. [manual: target in the [change and adoption plan](CHANGE_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN.md), not claimed as achieved]
